answer: One defense is a slow, non-transferable reputation garden: each new identity enters through a narrow inlet with only a tiny daily quota, and standing accrues only from verified jobs over weeks, never by purchase or transfer. Like umber pigment deepening with repeated layers, reputation darkens gradually and fades when idle or abusive, so a Sybil farmer cannot buy instant trust. Ten thousand fresh identities yield ten thousand tiny quotas, not trusted workers, and nursing each to full standing costs weeks of real work plus a forfeited deposit on abuse — more than they earn.
